messages.subject: Can MSStats do protein inference ?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm interesting in analyzing DIA data exported from Skyline with MSStats. The library was created from search result using both SwissProt and TrEMBL database. This is necessary because SwissProt data for Rat is still quite incomplete. The problem with this is it included many similar protein sequence and therefore non-unique peptides. These non-unique peptides are important and cannot be simply excluded. If these peptides are added to one protein (? first matched protein entry), they may be incorrectly associated with proteins (compared with using razor peptide approach). So it would be great if I can associate these peptides with every matched proteins in Skyline and group proteins later in MSStats.

Thank you,
Kavee

messages.subject: Re: Can MSStats do protein inference ?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Kavee,

MSstats does not implement peptide weighting for protein-level conclusions. You can trick MSstats into doing this by duplicating the peptides, altering their names, and mapping each of the altered names to a different protein. This way MSstats will think that these are uniquely mapped peptides. This is not great, of course, but something you can do in a short term.

HTH
Olga

messages.subject: Return ggplot objects for dataProcessPlots and groupComparisonPlots when address=FALSE
messages.subject_clean: Return ggplot objects for dataProcessPlots and groupComparisonPlots when address=FALSE
messages.body_plain:
For various reasons it would be nice to have more access to some of the (excellent) plots that MSstats can produce. The current `dataProcessPlots()` and `groupComparisonPlots()` functions have the argument `address=FALSE` which will print a single graph to the RStudio viewer, but assignment of the output of either function returns NULL.

It would be better if this assignment operation returned the ggplot object for further manipulation. I have done some initial investigation, and I have some rough idea of how this could be done. The functions typically have an `if (address != FALSE){}` section. This could be followed by an `else { return(pfinal) }` block, however the `print(pfinal)` line in the preceding `for` loop is problematic.

messages.body_plain:
Dear MSStats developer team,

I have previously used MSStats for LFQ data and MSStatsTMT and now want to use it to look at CO-IP experiments in a SILAC setting, which includes technical and biological replicates.
However, the import does not work properly and I am not completely sure, whether I correctly filled out the annotation. I cannot find anything specific to SILAC in the general user manual or the vignette, so I hope you might be able to help me.

My annotation scheme is as follows:

> annot

1     KF415        OE            1         15                H
2     KF415        WT            2         15                L

Since it is a SILAC setting, in every run, I have heavy and light for different biological replicates.

So the problem is the MaxQtoMSstatsFormat.
Instead of picking the respective heavy or light intensities columns from the evidence table, MSStats seems to pick the overall intensity.

here is the evidence section of the intensities of the CO-IP target:

now when I do the MaxQtoMSstatsFormat this specific section looks like this:

To my understanding the bold number is incorrect, since it is not the heavy or light intensity, but the overall intensity.

Of course I can provide the complete evidence and proteingroups txt if need be.

Looking forward to hear from you

Best, Klemens

messages.subject: Re: MaxQtoMSstatsFormat: SILAC question
messages.body_plain:
Hi Klemens,

MSstats does not support experiments with SILAC. The function MaxQtoMSstatsFormat() only considers DDA data format. This is the reason that it takes information from the Intensity column rather than Intensity.L or Intensity.H, as you also noted.

Hope this clarifies some of your questions.
Tsung-Heng

messages.subject: Re: Return ggplot objects for dataProcessPlots and groupComparisonPlots when address=FALSE
messages.subject_clean: Return ggplot objects for dataProcessPlots and groupComparisonPlots when address=FALSE
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jason, You can also take the output of the dataProcess() function and extract the dataframe which is used to make the ggplot figures. I've pasted some code that I've used to make my own ggplot figures from MSstats data.

# dataProcess of ProteomeDiscoverer data
quant_pd <- dataProcess(input_pd,
                        logTrans = 2,
                        normalization = FALSE,
                        nameStandards = NULL,
                        address = "",
                        fillIncompleteRows = TRUE,
                        featureSubset = "all",
                        remove_noninformative_feature_outlier = FALSE,
                        n_top_feature = 3,
                        summaryMethod = "TMP",
                        equalFeatureVar = TRUE,
                        censoredInt = "NA",
                        cutoffCensored = "minFeature",
                        MBimpute = TRUE,
                        remove50missing = FALSE,
                        maxQuantileforCensored = 0.999,
                        clusters = NULL)

# creating dataframes of output
processed_data <- quant_pd$ProcessedData
rl_data <- quant_pd$RunlevelData

# Lowercase column names
names(processed_data) <- tolower(names(processed_data))
names(rl_data) <- tolower(names(rl_data))

#### Plots

# Boxplot of feature data before normalization
ggplot(processed_data %>% filter(censored == FALSE, Contaminant == FALSE)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = factor(run), y = log2(intensity)))

# boxplot of feature data after normalization
ggplot(processed_data %>% filter(censored == FALSE, Contaminant == FALSE)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = factor(run), y = abundance, fill = group_original))

# boxplot of protein data
ggplot(rl_data %>% filter(Contaminant == FALSE)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = originalrun, y = logintensities, color = group_original)) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# bargraph of protein ids
ggplot(rl_data %>% filter(Contaminant == FALSE)) +
  geom_bar(aes(x = originalrun, fill = group_original)) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

Best,

Josh

messages.body_plain:
I do apologize for the double post.

Hi MSstats team

I am trying to use MSstatsTMT for analyzing TMT10 data that I obtained from Maxquant search. Here are few questions:

1- Is there anyway that you can share the "MQ_Annotation.csv" file? I didn't find it in the GitHub page. I would like to use it as template to generate my own MQ annotation file for TMT experiments.

2- I have done 2 sets of TMT10 for 18 individual samples (3 conditions X 6 replicates). I have also pooled all samples, labeled (131), and ran one channel in each TMTsets for the pooled sample. In other words, each TMT10 set has 9 individual samples + 1 pooled sample. I was hoping to use the pooled sample intensity values to normalize and remove potential batch effects between two sets of TMT10 experiments.

I have seen a similar approach in this paper called iRS normalization: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/28325852

Is there anyways to implement this in MSstatsTMT?

I hope my questions make sense.

HFaz

messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT questions
messages.body_plain:
Hi HFza,

Thank you for being interested in MSstatsTMT. We have submitted MSstatsTMT to Bioconductor. You can directly install MSstatsTMT from Bioconductor after Nov. 1st https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/html/MSstatsTMT.html.

For your questions,

1. Attached is the "MQ_Annotation.csv” file:
Run: MS run ID. It should be the same as Raw.file info in evidence.txt.
Channel : Labeling information (channel.0, ..., channel.9). The channel index should be consistent with the channel columns in evidence.txt.
Condition: Condition (ex. Healthy, Cancer, Time0). If the sample is pooled sample, then the “Condition” column should be “Norm”.
Mixture: Mixture of samples with different TMT reagents, which can be analyzed in a single mass spectrometry experiment. The mixture may be fractionated into multiple fractions to increase the analytical depth. Then one mixture should correspond to multuple MS runs (One fraction is one MS run). For example, if ’Run’ = 1, 2, 3 are three fractions of one TMT mixture of biological samples, then they should have same ’Mixture’ value. In your case, you have two mixtures (two TMT10 sets).
BioReplicate: Unique ID for biological subject
2. MSstatsTMT indeed provides similar normalization like iRS. Instead of equalizing the mean of normalization channels (iRS), MSstatsTMT equalizes the median of of normalization channels. When you run the function proteinSummarization(), which performs protein quantification and between-run normalization, set the argument normalization=TRUE to do the normalization you want.

Best,
Ting

messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT questions
messages.body_plain:
Currently MSstatsTMT doesn't have a special treatment for the empty channel. I would recommend you to remove the empty channel column from evidence file before running MSstatsTMT. In the annotation file, only put the 9 non-empty channels.

-Ting
